text:
maya: Running a cross-region routing failover test now. Noticing some pods in eu-west keep losing egress SNAT mappings when we flip GeoDNS -> latency steering. Can folks watch? :eyes:

deploy-bot: test-runner started job 2026-03-15T10:12Z (test-id: cr-failover-03)

ryan: saw a bunch of 502s from the LB in front of the redis cache during the flip. suspect connection resets because client IP changed?

linh: can you paste the LB logs? or tcpdump from a node?

maya: attaching short excerpt. these are from lb-a-eu-west logs when we toggled weight to us-east:
```
[10:15:23] client=10.12.8.90 -> backend=10.200.4.12 closing conn: conn_reset
[10:15:24] client=10.12.8.90 -> backend=10.200.4.13 new conn: established
[10:15:30] client=10.12.8.90 -> backend=10.200.4.12 timeout waiting for response
```

maya: the client IP above is the NATed egress from the worker pool. when we moved traffic, the source IP mapping sometimes changed mid-flow, which breaks sticky sessions for some stateful backends.

zane: oh yeah, our stateful services (redis-session and kv-locks) rely on source-IP based session affinity for a small % of traffic. we shouldnt rely on that across region shifts.

ryan: timeline: we switched geo-dns weights at 10:15:20, saw errors until 10:18. when we reverted, things healed. Latency steering was doing rapid weight changes due to health pings.

linh: do we have an easy mitigation? options I see: 1) preserve SNAT via stable egress IP per pod (hard), 2) disable source-IP affinity and use a cookie/token, 3) extend DNS TTL + drain window in routing controller, 4) use connection-aware global LB (but that's infra work).

maya: test notes: the routing controller does a 5s weight step for latency steering. that's probably too aggressive for backends with IP-affinity. i think we need a fallback policy: if backend returns >5% 5xx during a weight change, pause steering and roll back weights for 30s.

ops-bot: alert created: INC-2026-0315-krf (cross-region egress stickiness causing transient errors). Pager duty: on-call eng-infra.

zane: short-term patch: add a per-service annotation to disable IP-affinity for LB when region fallback is enabled. that'll make the steering safe for most. long-term: move affinity to an application token (session id) so egress NAT isn't a single point.

ryan: also flagging cost angle: keeping long DNS TTLs reduces flapping but increases imbalance/capacity pressure. for Dedicated customers we might want a region-pin option with guaranteed capacity vs latency steering that is aggressive.

linh: I'll open a PR to: 1) add the rollout safety guard in the routing-controller, 2) add a service annotation to force cookie-based affinity or disable IP-affinity.

maya: thanks. action items: @linh PR for controller + annotation, @zane create migration plan for session-token affinity, @ryan measure how many customers hit IP-affinity today (prod telemetry). We'll re-run test with 30s step and the safety guard.

ryan: quick config snippet I used locally to reproduce (kube svc + ip-affinity):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: kv-locks
  annotations:
    networking.redwood.io/affinity: "source_ip"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  sessionAffinity: ClientIP
```

maya: re-run scheduled at 10:50Z. Leaving running tests in the channel. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: test-runner finished job cr-failover-03: FAILURE (see INC-2026-0315-krf)

linh: opened PR #1247 with the safety guard and a config flag. cc @maya @ryan.

zane: created docs note for customers about region-pin vs latency-steer tradeoffs (link: https://internal.redwood/docs/region-routing).

maya: nice. we'll validate and then add to the playbook for cross-region ops. closing the loop after the follow-up test.
